messages:
Kevin (Sales): Hey @Ana, looping you in — Medirev legal asked for POC evidence: full audit logs for API key usage, key rotation records, and proof of delivery to their SIEM. They're doing a security review before we start Dedicated pool provisioning. Any blockers?
Ana (Eng): Hi Kevin — quick Q: is this going to be Hosted API keys for the POC or are we provisioning a Dedicated pool / Private VPC for them? That changes what we can export.
Kevin (Sales): They're open to Dedicated but want to see hosted first. Request says: 1) API key create/delete/rotate history 2) per-request request-id + requester ip 3) option to ship to Splunk/ S3 4) retention >= 90 days 5) KMS envelope details for keys.
Mike (Security): tagging requirements: we need to provide an exported manifest for key rotation (who, when, rotation job id), and HSM/KMS metadata (key origin, rotation schedule). For Hosted we can provide audit logs + KMS meta; for Dedicated we can additionally enable tenant-controlled KMS. Need to confirm whether Medirev requires customer-managed keys.
Jordan (SE): We can enable audit streaming to their Splunk HEC endpoint or export to an S3 bucket they control. Example Splunk HEC snippet we usually send:
```
POST https://<HEC_HOST>/services/collector/event/1.0
Authorization: Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>
{ "event": {"request_id": "{{request_id}}", "model": "gpt-3.x", "user": "redwood:api_key:abc"} }
```
Also we have an export job that zips JSON lines with full request metadata (timestamp, request_id, model, token_count, requester_ip) every 24h. Retention on our side is 180 days by default for Hosted; we can set a 90-day export for the POC.
Kevin (Sales): Nice — can we include key rotation logs too? Medirev wants a CSV or PDF evidence for the security questionnaire.
Ana (Eng): Yes. For Hosted API keys we have rotation audit events in our admin audit log. We can run an ad-hoc export for the POC window (start/end dates) and include: key_id, rotated_by, rotation_ts, old_key_hash (truncated), new_key_hash (truncated), rotation_ticket. We redact full secrets. Example line: `key_12345, alice.redwood, 2026-03-10T18:12:34Z, <sha256:xxxx>, <sha256:yyyy>, INC-2342`
Mike (Security): Add a note for the questionnaire: "Rotation processes use automated rotation jobs (cron + worker), logs capture operator identity via SSO (OKTA) and rotation job IDs. Secrets are never stored in plaintext; hashes are provided for evidence." We should also provide SOC2 artifact references and the control owners.
Kevin (Sales): Great. Medirev also asked about proof that api keys were disabled after POC and audit trail of that.
Jordan (SE): We can schedule a post-POC action: run a revoke job and export the revoke event id + timestamp. Command we typically run internally:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/keys/revoke -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"key_id":"key_12345"}'
```
poc-bot: Provisioned demo-hosted-medirev-01 (expires 2026-04-15) :rocket:
Ana (Eng): For Dedicated or Private, Ops will need an IP allowlist for their SIEM and an S3 bucket ARN (if they want S3 delivery). Also for Private we can hand over KMS CMK details (arn:aws:kms:...) but that requires an MOU and key policy alignment.
Mike (Security): Action items: 1) provide exported rotation CSV + redacted hashes 2) provide daily audit export (jsonl) for POC period 3) provide sample Splunk HEC forwarding config and network diagram 4) provide SOC2 control references and signed attestation template. I'll draft attestation text.
Kevin (Sales): Can someone draft the evidence bundle (zip) we can send to Medirev security by EOD tomorrow? Prefer PDF summary + CSV + sample logs.
Ana (Eng): I can generate the export and the PDF summary. Will need Medirev S3 write creds or Splunk HEC endpoint for live streaming. If they prefer email delivery, we can SFTP to their secure inbox.
Jordan (SE): I'll follow up with a templated README that explains each file in the bundle and the field definitions (request_id, ts, user, ip, model, tokens, rotation_ticket).
Mike (Security): I'll add the attestation and a short explanation of redaction policies.
Kevin (Sales): Awesome. @Medirev contact is carol@medirev.com — I'll ask them to provide S3 details or Splunk HEC and confirm CMK requirements. Thanks all :thumbsup:
